title: Lilah H.:
title_short: Lilah H. · Not a sports fan
headline: She does not watch sports. She still loves NBA Math Hoops, and math went from boring to fun.
story: Lilah plays volleyball and does not watch sports. She likes the game board and the pressure of a close game. Her last match was 20 to 21.
The turn: math was “kind of boring” before. Now it is “kind of fun” and she understands it more. This is the cut that shows Math Hoops is not only for sports kids. Protect it.

Loops: L1 “Why would a kid who doesn't watch sports love this?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:10 (“game boards… intense”). L2 “Did it change math for her?” opens at 0:17 and closes at 0:27. Stakes: math that feels boring.
do: Open on “I'm not really a sports fan” with the hook text already on screen.
Cut to girls playing on “game boards” so the viewer sees what she means.
Put the score “20 to 21” on screen as she says it.
Keep her before/after on math as one piece. It is the turn of the cut.
End on “I really like the challenge”, then the Donate end card.
dont: Do not use the school name she gives at the start.
Do not use the interviewer's name for her (“Nyla”). She is Lilah.
Do not use the rounding-decimals answer. It is hard to follow without the question.
No logo, name or fade at 0:00.
No end-of-year campaign words on the end card.

Interview mic into the camera. The gym was loud: kids are audible behind every answer. Keep a little room tone, it sells the day. Level pass and light noise reduction only.

-14 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP peak. Music always under the voice.
Pauses inside a bite longer than 0.7 s are cut to about 0.25 s. Row times in this plan count that.
Burned in, low in the frame, client font RangleRiforma Bold (brand kit in Airtable). Spell NBA Math Hoops (the auto-transcript writes “MBA”), Learn Fresh, WestEd.
Two H.264 MP4s: 16:9 1920×1080 and 9:16 1080×1920. Upload to Frame.io, then Ready for Review.
checklist: Frame 1 is the speaker with the hook text already on screen. No logo, no name, no fade at 0:00.
The hook text does not animate on.
The name super comes in at 00:03 or later, lower left, 2 s.
Captions spell NBA Math Hoops, never MBA.
No school names anywhere on screen.
The end card carries the call to action in this plan and nothing about the end-of-year campaign.
Two exports: 16:9 master and 9:16, same edit.
Student super is first name + last initial + grade only. Never a last name.
client_note: Why this matters: Learn Fresh asked for girls as well as boys and for kids who are not sports fans. Lilah is both. Her cut proves the game is not only for basketball kids.
